messages:
min.j: quick sync request 1: i'm prototyping a lightweight connector-lease flow for private tenants that need stable egress IPs without full dedicated endpoints. want quick opinions on backpressure and revocation semantics before i write the RFC.

omar_net: ok. big picture: mint short leases (tenant->relay) that include nat_ip + cert. relays honor leases. what are our safety/availability knobs?

min.j: proposal bullets:
- lease TTL: 10m by default
- renew endpoint: idempotent, cheap, accepts proof (jwt + client-sig)
- nat-pool: region-level sticky pool; leases consume an ip for session duration
- backpressure responses: ACCEPT / QUEUE (retry-after) / REJECT
- revoke: immediate -> draining window (default 60s) or force-revoke for security events

tess_ops: ops asks: how do we size nat pool and alert? metrics we need: nat_utilization, leases_active, renew_queue_len, revoke_lag. policy: autoscale pool up, alert at 80% and page at 95%.

omar_net: about queue: implement per-tenant soft-queue with queue-token redeemable once. QUEUE returns retry_after + token; token bound to connector pubkey to prevent replay. Also suggest a small per-relay burst slot to avoid DB roundtrips on spikes.

security-bot: security notes: revocation must be authoritative. if revocation stream partitions, default should be fail-closed for suspend/compromise events. for ops-level restarts we can fail-open with audit. cert TTL 1h, but we rotate often in practice. include cert_serial -> tenant mapping in audit logs.

min.j: failure modes: if nat_pool exhausted, options: (A) reject new leases, (B) spill to hosted control-plane for opt-in tenants. prefer (A) as default; allow spill with explicit opt-in flag.

tess_ops: agree. also need a console view mapping tenant -> current_lease (connector_id, nat_ip, expires_at, last_seen). make revoke/force-revoke one-click for support with audit trail.

omar_net: API sketch for renew:

POST /v1/lease/renew
Authorization: Bearer <short_jwt>
{ "tenant_id": "t-7", "connector_id": "c-9", "renew_nonce": "n-42" }

200 OK -> {status: ACCEPT, expires_at, nat_ip, cert}
202 QUEUE -> {status: QUEUE, retry_after, queue_token}
429 REJECT -> {status: REJECT, reason}

Keep renew idempotent and cheap; prefer local relay cache + async central allocator.

security-bot: also add per-tenant rate limits and circuit-breakers. relays must validate token binding and client signature before granting renew. log failed attempts for anomaly detection.

min.j: open questions i want in RFC: (1) default TTL 5/10/15m? (2) hold window for recently-expired leases (30/60/120s)? (3) queue overflow policy: reject vs hosted spill?

omar_net: my picks: 10m TTL, 60s hold, overflow -> reject default, allow hosted spill for opt-in.

tess_ops: +1, and add a per-customer policy toggle in console. i'll draft runbook and dashboards.

min.j: great, i'll write the RFC with APIs, metrics, and a 5-tenant canary plan. tagging @omar_net @tess_ops for review.
